reason: The cited evidence directly shows a 40-fold coercivity increase in FeCoNiMnCu after RTA and attributes it to magnetic anisotropy from anisotropic strain or chemical order, not dewetting. It also demonstrates L10 ordering with Pt addition. These findings accurately support the key premises, though the exact mechanism (chemical short-range order vs. strain) is suggested rather than definitively proven, which is a minor gap.
premises: RTA on FeCoNiMnCu thin films induces a 40-fold coercivity increase
Coercivity increase is due to induced magnetic anisotropy, not dewetting
Anisotropic strain or directional chemical order from RTA stabilizes magnetic anisotropy
RTA can induce L10 ordering in Pt-containing HEA films with high anisotropy
The mechanism is analogous to RTA-assisted synthesis of L10 FeCuPt
